description: A clone of the strace command for macOS

summary.one_liner: A Python-based system call tracer for macOS, modeled on Linux strace, that uses the LLDB debugger API and works with System Integrity Protection enabled.
summary.what_it_does: It runs a command or attaches to a running process (-p PID) and records its system calls, using LLDB's Python bindings to set breakpoints at syscall entry and exit, read registers for arguments, and decode them. Arguments are decoded symbolically, including flags, errno codes, and structs such as stat, sockaddr, and msghdr. Output can be strace-style text (to stdout or a file) or JSON Lines. Filtering works by syscall name or by category such as file, network, process, or memory, and -c prints summary statistics with time, call, and error counts. Color output is enabled when writing to a TTY. The README lists negation, regex, path, and fd filtering, follow-forks, and timestamp options as planned, not yet implemented.
use_cases: trace system calls made by a macOS program
debug file access of a command-line tool
see network syscalls made by curl or similar tools
profile syscall counts and errors with summary stats
trace a process without disabling SIP
capture strace-style logs as JSON for analysis
how_to_run: git clone https://github.com/Mic92/strace-macos (repository URL not fully shown in README)
notable: Works with System Integrity Protection enabled, unlike dtruss
Pure Python with no kernel extensions or compiled components
Category-based syscall filtering (file, network, process, and more)
JSON Lines output alongside strace-compatible text output
caveats: Beta status; multi-threading, follow-forks, and several filters and timestamp options are planned but not implemented
Requires macOS 12+ and must run under the macOS system Python (/usr/bin/python3) because LLDB bindings do not work with Homebrew, pyenv, or Nix Python
Apple Silicon is the primary platform; Intel support is work in progress
keywords: see what files a program opens
